To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a directly depicting ontology of type SNAP (snapshot ontology) is an ontology that is built on top of a set of categories that are all of type SNAP, and (2) a directly depicting of type SPAN (spanning ontology) is an ontological theory built on top of categories all of which are of type SPAN.

(i) the theory of directly describing ontologies is based on the notion of a category and that (ii) it is possible to construct directly depicting ontologies of type span and snap, which (iii) can be combined into a single ontology.

(a) directly depicting ontologies can be axiomatized in a simple, elegant way that is compatible with the basic principles of the theory of regions; (b) the meta-ontology of the theory of depicting ontologies is a theory of regions; and (c) depicting ontologies are ontologies of type 2.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
directly depicting ontologies are the ontologies that are needed in order to be able to describe the reality as it is.
directly depicting ontologies are a powerful and flexible tool for the representation of spatio-temporal reality.
the theory of directly representing ontologies provides a powerful and elegant framework for the representation of spatio-temporal phenomena and for the integration of different kinds of information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new approach to the ontology of space and time that is based on the distinction between perduring and enduring entities and that is powerful enough for describing both.

we have provided the conceptual foundations for a new kind of ontology, one that can be used in the description of complex, dynamic, spatially extended processes, and the entities that participate therein, and that is powerful enough, at the same time, to describe enduring entities as they are in the world.
we have provided an ontological framework that allows for the description of the spatio-temporal world in a uniform way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single ontology language is not powerful enough to represent the full complexity of reality.
a single theory is sufficient to account for the ontology of both enduring and perduring entities.
the two complementary ontologies of type span and SNAP, which are both based on the same meta-ontological framework, can be used to model complex processes and enduring entities in a unified way.
